title: Run the Numbers on Who You're Actually Choosing

sections.title: Count the Messages
prompt: Scroll to a chat thread with someone you're chasing. Count your messages vs. theirs — write the actual ratio down.
Now open a thread with someone who's asked about your week twice and you never replied. When did you last respond to them?
What's the emotional word you'd use for the first person's silence — and is 'exciting' or 'anxious' closer to the truth?
Name one specific unremarkable thing the second person did for you that you brushed past at the time.

sections.title: Check If It's Them or the Chase
prompt: Think of a time an unavailable person suddenly became available. Did your interest in them survive past a few weeks? What actually happened to it?
Write down what you're chasing in one sentence — is it their company, or the moment they finally text back?
What's the 'open loop' here — the specific question their silence keeps leaving unanswered in your head?
If they replied to everything tomorrow with total warmth, what would you talk about? If you're stuck, that's the answer.

sections.title: Find the Boring, Reliable Ones
prompt: List two or three people who've shown up for something inconvenient — a bad week, a hospital visit, a stressful project — without you asking.
For each, when did you last give them your full attention instead of a distracted reply?
The blog's test: 'wait and watch what they actually do over time.' Pick one person you're unsure about — what have their actions actually shown you in the last month, regardless of what they've said?
What's one thing you could do this week that isn't just a thank-you text, but actually matches the effort they've put in?

sections.title: Find the Role You're Auditioning People For
prompt: Have you cut off an unavailable person before and found a near-identical dynamic within a few months? Name the pattern if so.
Whose approval currently feels like it would 'prove' something about you? Write down what exactly it would prove.
Why does affection from people who already love you feel like it 'doesn't count' — where did that discount come from?
What's one place you already get real evidence of your own worth that has nothing to do with anyone's approval?

cta: Reply with your actual message ratio from Section 1 — the real number, from the real thread. I'll tell you what mine was.
